第 17 章 Distributed Teams Are Founded on Explicit Communication Channels分布式团队建立在明确的沟通渠道之上

Juan Pablo Buriticá / 胡安·帕布罗·布里蒂卡

— 第 58 页 —

All teams past a certain size become distributed. It could be across rooms, floors, buildings or cities. If you manage a team in a company that is growing fast, you will run into this challenge. By being deliberate and explicit about the communication channels used, your teams will be more productive, easier to manage, and able to grow faster. With the increasing popularity of remote work, understanding how to rely on different channels, especially written ones, will also enable you to be better prepared if your team eventually becomes distributed.

所有超过一定规模的团队都会变成分布式的。可能是跨房间、跨楼层、跨楼或跨城市。如果你在一家快速成长的公司管理团队，你会遇到这个挑战。通过有意识地、明确地使用沟通渠道，你的团队会更高效、更容易管理、成长更快。随着远程工作越来越流行，理解如何依赖不同渠道（尤其是书面渠道）也会让你在团队最终变成分布式时准备更充分。

The primary benefit of choosing explicit communication types and channels for information is increased productivity. When team members aren't clear on where to find the information, their productivity is affected. They might waste a few hours trying to guess where to find it or, if they're good at asking questions, go around creating unnecessary focus interruptions for their team members. That poorly timed tap on the shoulder or chat app notification during deeply focused programming can be prevented if you are explicit on where and how information can be found.

为信息选择明确的沟通类型和渠道的主要好处是提高生产力。当团队成员不清楚在哪里找信息时，他们的生产力就会受影响。他们可能浪费几个小时猜信息在哪，或者如果他们善于问问题，就会到处给团队成员造成不必要的专注打断。如果你明确信息在哪里、怎么找，深度编程时那种不合时宜的拍肩膀或聊天通知就可以避免。

A good way of reducing interruptions is to choose asynchronous communication channels for nonblocking items and helping team members review them on a cadence. For example, architectural decisions and discussions can begin as long-form documents with an established period of comments, also known as Request For Comments (RFCs). These can eventually be used as onboarding materials or blueprints for future systems. Asynchronous communication is best for situations in which real-time dialog is not necessary. Communicating status, reviewing code, broadcasting organizational changes, and the resolution of questions that are not urgent are well suited for asynchronous channels like collaborative documents, forums, task-tracking tools, and email.

减少打断的一个好方法是为非阻塞事项选择异步沟通渠道，帮团队成员按节奏查看。例如，架构决策和讨论可以以长文档形式开始，设定一段评论期，也就是 RFC（意见征求）。这些最终可以作为入职材料或未来系统的蓝图。异步沟通最适合不需要实时对话的场景。同步状态、评审代码、广播组织变更、解决不紧急的问题，都很适合协作文档、论坛、任务跟踪工具和邮件等异步渠道。

— 第 59 页 —

When the real-time exchange of ideas is crucial, it's more appropriate to choose synchronous communication channels like group chats, in-person meetings, or video calls. Grooming a backlog over email, or discussing strategy on a forum or a group chat when different members are busy will probably not lead to a timely outcome. For situations like this, you want to get your teams on a cadence so that they can block their time on the calendar and be present. This is especially important if you are spread across timezones.

当实时思想交流至关重要时，更适合选择群聊、面对面会议或视频通话等同步沟通渠道。通过邮件梳理待办列表、或者在论坛或群聊里讨论策略而不同成员都在忙，可能不会及时出结果。这种情况下，你要让团队有固定节奏，这样他们可以在日历上block出时间、在场参与。如果你们跨时区，这一点尤其重要。

Multichannel chats have gained popularity because they can be used both synchronously and asynchronously. The good use of these tools can have a positive impact on the productivity of a team, but it can also have a detrimental effect if you set an expectation of always being present. Deep focus time is greatly affected when this happens. You can prevent your teams from falling into this behavior if you are explicit about the broadcasting of important information so that team members can disconnect. For example, set up a read-only announcement channel or agree on "quiet hours." Having clear protocols for incident management and conflict resolution can also alleviate the need to be constantly present, in case something important happens.

多渠道聊天工具越来越流行，因为它们可以同步也可以异步使用。用好这些工具对团队生产力有积极影响，但如果你设定了「永远在线」的期望，也会有负面影响。深度专注时间在这种情况下会受到很大影响。如果你明确重要信息的广播方式，团队成员就可以断联，从而防止团队陷入这种行为。例如，设立只读公告频道或约定「安静时间」。有清晰的事件管理和冲突解决流程也可以减轻必须时刻在线的需要——即使有重要的事发生。

When you build teams that rely on being in the same location to get access to information, you make it easier for information gaps to proliferate when team members are absent or the team outgrows the space. Information gaps create misalignment, and in turn, you need to spend more time managing communication. By defaulting to written communication channels from the beginning, you make it easier to distribute information that is clear and enables alignment.

当你建立依赖在同一地点才能获取信息的团队时，团队成员缺席或团队超出空间时，信息缺口更容易扩散。信息缺口造成不一致，反过来你需要花更多时间管理沟通。从一开始就默认使用书面沟通渠道，你就能更容易地分发清晰、能促成对齐的信息。

One final benefit of investing in explicit communication channels from the beginning is setting up your team for fast growth. When communication practices become standards, events like adding new members to the team are less taxing on the group. For example, if you have a good set of RFCs that cover important past technical decisions and the discussions around them, new hires can understand the trade-offs you had to make. They might even have architectural diagrams or system contracts that are kept up to date with the evolution of your systems. A 90-day onboarding checklist template is another great example. You can use it as an evolving document to which new hires contribute as they navigate their first weeks in your team, making the next hire's experience much better.

从一开始就投资明确沟通渠道的最后一个好处是为团队快速成长做好准备。当沟通实践成为标准时，加新成员这类事情对团队的负担就更小。例如，如果你有一套好的 RFC，涵盖过去重要的技术决策及其讨论，新员工就能理解你做过的权衡。它们甚至可能有架构图或系统契约，随着系统演进保持更新。90 天入职清单模板是另一个好例子。你可以把它作为一个不断演化的文档，新员工在入职头几周使用时也可以贡献内容，让下一个新员工的体验更好。

— 第 60 页 —

Relying on in-person communication in the early days of your team is low friction and convenient, but it can bring your team to a halt if it grows beyond the limitations of physical space. If instead you build a culture of being explicit about the communication types and channels used and lean into written mediums you can build teams that are resilient to fast change. Thanks to the internet, written communications are accessible and aren't subject to the limitations of physical presence, serendipitous encounters by the seltzer machine, or inconvenient taps on the shoulder.

团队早期依赖面对面沟通摩擦小、方便，但如果团队成长到超出物理空间限制，就会让团队停滞。相反，如果你建立一种明确沟通类型和渠道的文化、倾向书面媒介，你就能建立对快速变化有韧性的团队。多亏了互联网，书面沟通是可访问的，不受物理在场、气泡水机旁的偶遇、或者不合时宜的拍肩膀的限制。
